A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Agent Distillation work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated material and v2's additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original teacher/student experiments on eight reasoning benchmarks, component analyses, and qualitative failure cases.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds student-model comparisons, ablations, temperature tests, and repeated-inference results.

M1.justification: The distillation objective, first-thought prefix (FTP), and self-consistent action generation (SAG) remain unchanged. v2 specifies what happens when every sampled action fails; this documents a previously unspecified implementation case rather than establishing an algorithm revision.

E1.justification: Training still uses HotpotQA and MATH, and evaluation retains the same eight factual and mathematical benchmarks. The additional model and sensitivity experiments introduce no new datasets, task requirements, or input environments.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds SAG-only agent variants without FTP. New Table 8 compares full fine-tuning against LoRA. Existing CoT prompting, CoT distillation, RAG, and general-versus-code-specific model comparisons are retained; the newly cited tool-use methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The main splits, metrics, training budgets, and inference defaults remain unchanged. Additional experiments introduce Llama-3.2-1B and Phi-4-mini student configurations, a temperature sweep from 0.2 to 1.0, and full fine-tuning for two epochs at learning rate 1e-5. These extend the evaluation rather than replace its existing protocol.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: SAG-only rows isolate component effects, Table 4 tests dependence on student model family, Appendix D.4 examines temperature sensitivity and inference randomness, and D.5 compares full fine-tuning with LoRA. The original error, retrieval, token-count, and qualitative case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 reports means and standard deviations across five inference seeds for 0.5B, 1.5B, and 3B agents on AIME (Table 7). This is a targeted uncertainty analysis, not evidence of repeated training or uncertainty estimates across the full benchmark suite.

E6.justification: Existing scores in Tables 2–3 and the teacher-performance table are retained. v2 adds SAG-only, Llama/Phi, temperature, seed-variation, and full-fine-tuning results. For example, new Table 8 reports average accuracy of 26.24 for full fine-tuning versus the retained LoRA result of 29.11. These are additional comparisons, not improved replacements for earlier scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same distillation objectives and trajectory definitions. Neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs, and v2's expanded mechanism discussion introduces no new formal assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: distilling tool-using agents, improving them through FTP and SAG, and matching larger CoT-distilled models across eight benchmarks. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 reframes FTP's motivation around interference with learned CoT reasoning, adds a model-size explanation for MATH500 behavior, and interprets temperature sensitivity and full fine-tuning results. Appendix A adds specific concerns about harmful code execution and possible safeguards. Its earlier Qwen-only limitation remains despite the new model-family experiments.

D1.justification: v2 specifies LoRA application to all linear layers, random selection of a failed action when all SAG candidates fail, and error feedback for subsequent correction. It also documents the full-fine-tuning settings and states that reproduction code accompanies the supplement. The approximately 2,000 filtered trajectories were already disclosed in v1's Appendix C.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds brief coverage of earlier tool-use work, including Toolformer, TinyAgent, and function-calling/self-training approaches. References also add Phi-4-mini and OpenHands. The positioning around distilling much smaller agents remains stable; HarmAug's publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. Changes include a rewritten FTP motivation, additional analysis paragraphs and Appendix D.4–D.5, an appended NeurIPS checklist, and edits to terminology, affiliations, acknowledgments, and conference information.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially through four new tables covering model families, temperatures, seed variation, and fine-tuning, plus SAG-only rows in Table 2. Figure 2 moves before the introduction, and existing plots are redistributed. All eight original figures and the renumbered teacher-performance table are retained.

improvement.justification: The added component controls and Llama/Phi experiments improve attribution and address v1's lack of validation beyond Qwen; temperature and seed checks strengthen robustness evidence. However, new Table 4 contains inconsistent averages: the Llama+FTP scores average 22.05, whereas 22.93 is reported. Appendix A also still claims that only Qwen was tested, and uncertainty analysis remains confined to AIME inference. These reporting weaknesses limit the overall gain without negating the useful additional evidence.
